headline: Vision Conclave 5.0 | Vision Conclave Uttar Pradesh
content: As India advances towards Viksit Bharat @ 2047, Uttar Pradesh has emerged as one of the country’s most ambitious growth engines. As India advances towards Viksit Bharat @ 2047, Uttar Pradesh has emerged as one of the country’s most ambitious growth engines. With the vision of becoming a USD 1 trillion economy, the state is simultaneously leading transformative initiatives across Artificial Intelligence, Digital Public Infrastructure, Electronics Manufacturing, Semiconductor ecosystem development, Defence Manufacturing, Data Centres, Logistics, Smart Governance and Future Skills. The Government’s recent launch of the Uttar Pradesh AI Mission, Electronics Component Manufacturing Policy 2025, AI-enabled Nivesh Mitra 3.0, emerging data centre ecosystem, semiconductor investments and focus on digital entrepreneurship reflect a decisive shift from digital governance to AI-powered governance and innovation-led economic growth. Against this backdrop, the 5th Edition of ETGovernment Vision Conclave seeks to create a national platform for showcasing Uttar Pradesh’s next phase of transformation, from policy formulation to implementation, from investment commitments to execution and from digital governance to AI-driven public service delivery. Unlock the future of energy at the "Vision Conclave 5.0 2026" Dive into an extraordinary event where visionary ideas are sparked, innovation thrives, and energy possibilities are unleashed beyond imagination. “By 2047, Uttar Pradesh will be a state that is economically self-reliant, culturally rich, and socially just.” – Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath With India’s ambitious goal of becoming a $30 trillion economy by 2047, Uttar Pradesh aims to contribute significantly by expanding its economy to $6 trillion by the same year. Aligned with the vision of both the Government of India and the Uttar Pradesh Government, ETGovernment – The Economic Times is proud to present the 5th Edition of the Vision 2047 Conclave, themed “Viksit Bharat, Viksit Uttar Pradesh”, scheduled for November 2026 in Lucknow. Showcase Innovations: Highlight cutting-edge AI technologies and solutions that are reshaping industries and public services. Foster Collaboration: Facilitate discussions and partnerships among government officials, private sector leaders, academic experts, and AI practitioners. Strategize Development: Develop actionable strategies to enhance the AI ecosystem in Uttar Pradesh and promote sustainable growth and innovation. Promote AI City Vision: Outline the blueprint for the AI City in Lucknow, focusing on infrastructure, investment opportunities, and collaborative platforms. In alignment with the Government of India’s strategic vision for AI and technological advancement, the Government of Uttar Pradesh is embarking on a ground breaking initiative to establish the country’s first AI city in Lucknow. This pioneering project aims to cultivate a vibrant AI ecosystem and position the state as a leading technology hub. The Uttar Pradesh Event & Conclave represents a pivotal moment in the state’s journey toward becoming a leading AI hub. By bringing together diverse stakeholders, the conclave aims to foster innovation, collaboration, and strategic planning, setting the stage for a new era of AI-driven growth and development in Uttar Pradesh.

headline: PM’s speech at the launch of development projects in Banaskantha, Gujarat
content: Popular Chief Minister of Gujarat Shri Bhupendra Bhai Patel, Deputy Chief Minister Bhai Harsh Sanghvi ji, Speaker of the Legislative Assembly Shri Shankarbhai Chaudhary, all ministers of the Gujarat Government, Members of Parliament and Members of the Legislative Assembly, other public representatives, brothers and sisters. Today, through technology, farmers from every district of the country are connected with us. Today, through technology, farmers from every village of Gujarat are connected with us. Chief Ministers of different states, ministers, all of them are with us today in this important programme for farmers. I heartily welcome all of them as well. Today, Banaskantha has established its stature. Just now, I was watching on the screen that perhaps such a large gathering seated on charpoys has never been held anywhere in the world. For the people of the country too, it must be an amazing sight that everyone in this gathering is seated on charpoys. Today, Banaskantha has revived this great tradition of our villages. Had you informed the Guinness Book of World Records in advance, they would certainly have recorded it as a world record. It was just mentioned here a moment ago. The responsibility that you entrusted to me has now completed twenty-five years. And look at the coincidence, after completing twenty-five years, my first visit has been to our Banaskantha. Let me remind you that after becoming Chief Minister in 2001, my first major public programme as Chief Minister was held in Deesa. The older people here will remember that Lok Kalyan Mela. That programme was perhaps historic. Three lakh people from a single district attended it. I do not believe that record has been broken to this day. That record belongs to Banaskantha. The journey began there, and today I have got the opportunity to present an account of twenty-five years of service at the same place. Only a few days after Navratri, I have received the opportunity to come to the sacred land of Mother Amba. I bow at the feet of Mother Amba. A short while ago, projects dedicated to women, children, farmers, and livestock rearers were inaugurated and foundation stones laid here. A new instalment of PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi has also reached the accounts of crores of small farmers across the country. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to the people of Gujarat, to the people of the country, and to farmers across India. The people of Gujarat and Banaskantha should forgive me, but I have to speak in Hindi today because people from all over the country are connected with this programme. You permit me to speak in Hindi, don’t you? Very good.

headline: Space Conversation | Maharashtra’s Space-Aerospace-Defence Investment Landscape
content: The state of Maharashtra is the leading sub-national economy of the Republic of India. With robust lay out of public infrastructure, conducive policies from the central and state governments, and a steady supply of highly-skiilled and young work force, Maharashtra is aiming to reach state domestic gross product of USD 1 trillion in the next few years. The state has identified space, aerospace and defence as main pillar of its growing economy, taking into consideration the central government’s Aatmanirbhar Bharat vision. Maharashtra enjoys the presence of strategic military and non-military infrastructure that now aids in ensuring industrial production from within the state contributes to national requirements in large volumes and with tunable supply cadence. The recent wars fought all across the world, including India’s Operation Sindoor, has demonstrated the criticality of new-age innovations in the fighting of next wars. Better equipped and secure weaponry and military C4ISR systems are central to winnings of battles and wars. However, that continuous innovation is only possible through funding mechanisms that are capable of forecasting the warfare trends, anticipating the shocks in supply chains, ensuring contigencies, and determining the obsolescence of weapons and C4ISR systems so as to not compromise the interests of the nation. In this regard, Maharashtra is developing a vast innovation-manufacturing-testing network which requires continuous innovations and the same calls for identifying new financing measures. This ORF Space Conversation will discuss what are some of the state-of-the-art projects that are appearing on the soil of Maharashtra, and what type of financing mechanisms are being attempted to ensure that full life cycle of innovation is financed domestically and via reliable international partners. Managing Partner, Bharat Emerging and Strategic Technology Fund

headline: PM lays the foundation stone, inaugurates and dedicates to the Nation development projects worth over ₹14,000 Crore in Banaskantha, Gujarat
content: From farms and dairy to infrastructure and connectivity, Banaskantha is making new strides in development: PM Our farmers, our Annadatas, are one of the strongest pillars of a Viksit Bharat, and our government has always prioritized the welfare of farmers and their empowerment: PM Animal husbandry forms a vital pillar of our rural economy; Over the last decade, we have also heavily emphasized leveraging science and technology in this sector and dairy: PM We are making animal husbandry not just a tradition, but a strong instrument to increase farmers’ income and bring prosperity to our villages: PM Until the final moment of my life, I will remain devoted only to your service: PM Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi laid the foundation stone, inaugurated, and dedicated to the nation development projects worth over ₹14,000 crore today in Banaskantha, Gujarat. headline: Maharashtra govt fixes rates for PET-CT, MRI contrast; eligible poor patients to get free tests
content: Mumbai, The Maharashtra government on Thursday fixed rates for PET-CT scans and contrast agents used in CT and MRI tests at government medical colleges and hospitals, introducing three categories of patients to streamline charges and ensure eligible beneficiaries receive free services.The decision of the state Medical Education Department comes amid confusion over charges at facilities operating under the public-private partnership (PPP) model, where rates for PET-CT (Positron Emission Tomography - Computed Tomography) scans and contrast agents were not clearly defined, said a government order.Many economically weaker patients depend on government-run medical colleges and hospitals for treatment, including advanced diagnostic tests. The government has now specified the rates and payment procedures to bring uniformity across these facilities, it said."Under the new order, a whole-body PET-CT scan, with or without intravenous contrast, will cost Rs 10,250 for paying patients. The charge includes FDG, a substance used in the scan, and is 50 per cent lower than the Rs 20,500 package rate under Mahatma Jyotirao Phule Jan Arogya Yojana (MJPJAY)," the government resolution (GR) said.The government has fixed the rate for contrast agents used in CT scans at Rs 420 for 50 ml and Rs 830 for 100 ml. The charge for 10 ml of gadolinium-based contrast used in MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) scans has been set at Rs 950, it said.The order classifies patients into three categories: those eligible for free services, paying patients, and sponsored or referred patients.Eligible patients will not be charged for the prescribed investigations. Beneficiaries covered under MJPJAY and the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) will also receive the specified tests free of cost under the respective schemes.Patients who do not qualify for free services will pay the applicable charges through the hospital's billing desk. Sponsored or referred patients will be charged according to the full rates specified in agreements with service providers, the order stated.The government said the rates were finalised after a comparative assessment, as the absence of fixed charges had led to variations in the amounts collected by different institutions."To prevent further confusion, all payments must be made through the hospital's billing desk. Patients and their relatives cannot pay private service providers directly, either in cash or online. Violations could invite action under the terms of the agreement," it said.Hospitals have been directed to display the rates and payment procedures prominently in Marathi and English. The order takes immediate effect and applies to PET-CT facilities operated under the PPP model at government medical colleges and hospitals.

headline: West Bengal government warns of strict action against violations of firecracker norms on Diwali, Chhath
content: Kolkata The West Bengal government on Thursday (October 29, 2026) announced that it will take strict action against people violating the firecracker norms during Diwali and Chhath Puja. The police have also arrested one man for wrongfully hoarding banned crackers and recovered around 110 kg crackers. “The accused was arrested from the spot at about 01:45 hrs on 29.10.2026, and the firecrackers were seized in the presence of witnesses following due legal formalities,” a statement from Kolkata Police said on Thursday (October 29, 2026). A suo motu case was registered by a police officer at the Burrabazar Police Station, after which 19-year-old Md. Toufiq was arrested. The Director General of Police, West Bengal, Siddhi Nath Gupta, also said that people will not be allowed to use sky lanterns without acquiring proper permission from the fire department. “They can be sold, bought, and used, but if you want to use them, acquire permission and follow the due process,” Mr. Gupta said. They also added that only green crackers will be allowed and that they have multiple methods in place to ensure sellers do not have fake green cracker labels on their products. The Home Secretary, Sanghamitra Ghosh urged that the use of green crackers should also be limited. Curbing pollution Meanwhile, Ms. Ghosh urged people to comply with pollution-control regulations for a better environment and said that they have launched an awareness campaign to make people understand that celebrations and festivals can also happen without polluting crackers. “It is not just about enforcement; it is also a lot about self-awareness. Every single person gets affected by this pollution,” Ms. Ghosh also said. Ms. Ghosh said the decibel limit was 125 and 90 for sound-emitting and light-emitting crackers, respectively. On Diwali, the time limit for bursting crackers is between 8 and 10 p.m. and on Chhath Puja, from 6 to 8 a.m. They also added that surveillance and patrolling will be higher during the festival days. “We will inspect all storage and manufacturing points, and keep a watch on the cracker markets to ensure no violations are made,” Ms. Ghosh added. EOM

content: !Image 1: Commercial-Tax Commissioner-cum-Secretary Amit Kumar said the new system integrator will develop an 'Integrated Revenue Intelligence System' (IRIS) by establishing inter-departmental integration. Commercial-Tax Commissioner-cum-Secretary Amit Kumar said the new system integrator will develop an 'Integrated Revenue Intelligence System' (IRIS) by establishing inter-departmental integration. The Jharkhand government on Thursday signed an agreement with Choice Consultancy Services Pvt Ltd, a new system integrator, to enhance revenue collection capacity and curb leakage, an official said. The agreement was signed here in the presence of Jharkhand finance minister Radhakrishna Kishore. "The objective of this agreement is to make the functioning of the Commercial Tax Department more effective, transparent, and technology-based. Through the new system, significant steps will be taken toward strengthening tax administration, simplifying processes, and enhancing efficiency in departmental operations," Kishore said in a post on X in Hindi.

headline: MSDE and Government of Madhya Pradesh sign MoU to establish Skill India International Centre in Bhopal
content: The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India, and the Government of Madhya Pradesh signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in New Delhi to strengthen collaboration for international skill development and overseas employment opportunities. The MoU was signed by Ms. Manasi Sahay Thakur, Joint Secretary, International Cooperation, MSDE, and Shri Manish Singh, Principal Secretary, Department of Technical Education, Skill Development and Employment, Government of Madhya Pradesh. The partnership will facilitate the establishment of a Skill India International Centre (SIIC) at Sant Shiromani Ravidas Global Skills Park, Bhopal, who will also be managing the Centre on behalf of Government of Madhya Pradesh. The Centre will help bridge gaps between domestic training curricula and the occupational competencies, language proficiency and certification standards required by overseas employers for identified job roles. The initiative aligns with the Government’s vision of creating pathways for Indian youth to access international employment opportunities and contribute to Viksit Bharat @ 2047. Expressing her views on the partnership, Smt. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, MSDE, said, “The establishment of the Skill India International Centre in Bhopal strengthens our efforts to equip the youth of Madhya Pradesh with globally relevant skills and connect them to international employment opportunities. By aligning training with employer-validated demand, destination-country standards and language requirements, the Centre will strengthen candidates’ employability in international markets. This partnership reflects our commitment to building an ethical, transparent and responsive overseas mobility ecosystem that supports workers throughout their skilling to employment journey.” Under the collaboration, the Government of Madhya Pradesh will manage the Centre’s day-to-day operations, staffing, infrastructure and local implementation, while MSDE will provide national guidelines, technical support, digital infrastructure and coordination for demand identification and overseas employment pathways. The SIIC will function as a state-level coordination hub for candidate mobilisation, country-specific training, foreign-language capacity, cultural orientation, pre-departure preparation and linkages with skilling institutions and international partners. Implementation will be monitored against agreed Key Performance Indicators, including the number of overseas-employment-ready candidates tagged, growth in the trained workforce for priority corridors, international placements, year-on-year placement growth and remittance growth. Financial and performance progress will be reviewed periodically, with continued support linked to approved work plans, budgets, utilisation certificates, reporting compliance and achievement of agreed milestones.

headline: Population enumeration during Census 2027 to be held from Jan 25 to Feb 28, self-enumeration from Jan 10: MHA
content: New Delhi: Population enumeration during Census 2027 will be held in most of India between January 25 and February 28 next year with self enumeration starting from January 10, a notification issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs said on Friday. The population enumeration in snow-bound areas of Uttarakhand, Jammu and Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh will be conducted between September 1 and would end on September 30 while it will be undertaken in Goa, Uttar Pradesh and Punjab as well as in places other than snowbound areas in Uttarakhand from December 1 to January 4, the MHA had said earlier. The rest of the country will witness the population enumeration -- second phase of Census 2027 -- will be held between January 25 and February 28 with a revisional round scheduled between March 1 and March 5. The self enumeration phase will be between January 10 and 24. .The reference date for the Census 2027 be 00:00 hours of the first day of March 2027, the notification said. The government had earlier notified 40 questions to be asked during the population enumeration phase , including one to record caste – a first in independent India – as provided by the respondent. The questions -- as against 29 in the last Census in 2011 -- also include fresh ones like details of place of Covid-19 vaccination, number of bank accounts, digital literacy status, nationality as declared, spouse's name as also mobile number, Aadhaar number, Voter ID number and passport number if available. Earlier in the day, Congress General Secretary (Communications) Jairam Ramesh alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah were "orchestrating" Census 2027 in a way that it could determine citizenship, and asserted that this is "blatantly illegal". Referring to a media report, which claimed that an enumerator at a training session explained how to coax respondents to share Aadhaar data, Ramesh said, "This is truly extraordinary and reveals how diabolical the PM-HM duo are. First, they have got the ECI to determine citizenship which is brazenly illegal. Now they are orchestrating Census 2027 in a way so as to determine citizenship. This is blatantly illegal." In the first phase of Census operations, which is the House-Listing Operation (HLO), details related to the housing conditions, assets and amenities of each household will be collected while in the second phase, when population is counted, demographic, socio-economic, cultural and other details of every person in each household will be collected.

content: The Gulf conflict has disrupted global supply chains, pushed... REITs have changed the way commercial real estate is owned a... What really powers the cloud? Behind every Google search, A... Luxury real estate is one of the most talked-about segments ... Himachal Pradesh Assembly Speaker Shri Kuldeep Singh Pathania has urged Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Shri Nitin Gadkari to grant National Highway status to a strategic road corridor linking Shahpur, Draman, Singhuta, Chuwari, Chamba, Jot, Tissa, Sach and Pangi. During a meeting in New Delhi, he also sought approval for a tunnel between Chuwari and Chamba, citing the route’s importance for defence logistics, regional connectivity and tourism. Shri Gadkari said the Centre was finalising its policy and criteria for declaring new National Highways and that the proposal would be considered after the guidelines were completed. Himachal Pradesh Assembly Speaker Shri Kuldeep Singh Pathania has sought the Centre’s approval to designate a strategic road corridor connecting Dharamshala, Chamba and the remote Pangi region as a National Highway. He raised the demand during a meeting with Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Shri Nitin Gadkari in New Delhi on October 26, submitting a written representation seeking early consideration of the proposal. The Assembly Speaker highlighted the route’s strategic significance for the Indian Army’s divisional headquarters at Yol Cantonment near Dharamshala. According to his representation, the corridor could facilitate the movement of troops and military equipment towards border areas during a security emergency. He argued that developing only selected stretches would not meet the wider strategic objective of establishing a more comprehensive road connection to the region. The Chamba–Tissa–Bairagarh–Sach section is already under consideration by the Centre for development through the General Reserve Engineer Force (GREF). Shri Pathania requested that the proposal be extended to include the Draman–Singhuta–Chuwari–Chamba stretch via Jot, so that the wider route towards Pangi could be considered as part of the National Highway network. He also told the Union minister that the Shahpur/Draman–Chuwari–Chamba road via Jot had already been widened with support from the World Bank and the Central Infrastructure Fund, and had reached nearly double-lane standards. In response, Shri Gadkari said the central government was in the final stages of deliberations on the policy for declaring new National Highways. He indicated that the proposal would be considered once the new guidelines and criteria were finalised. No final approval for National Highway status was announced following the meeting. The proposed corridor is expected to improve connectivity between Gaggal Airport, Shahpur, Chamba and Pangi, reducing travel difficulties for residents of remote areas. Better road access could also support tourism and improve the movement of essential supplies and security personnel. The proposal remains subject to the Centre’s policy framework and approval process. Its eventual scope will depend on whether the government accepts the request to include the wider corridor, alongside the proposed Chuwari–Chamba tunnel, in future infrastructure planning.
